image_description: A close-up, macro shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra). The image focuses on the head and upper torso. The subject displays the characteristic glossy black skin with large, irregular bright yellow patches. The eye is visible, dark and protruding. The skin texture appears wet and glandular. A portion of a forelimb is visible in the lower left, showing black skin with yellow markings. The background is out-of-focus earthy tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and flattened with prominent parotoid glands (poison glands) behind the eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with the species, appearing broad. The area behind the eye shows the characteristic swelling associated with parotoid glands, though the extreme close-up makes precise anatomical definition slightly difficult, the general morphology matches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are small, dark, and protruding with gold-flecked irises.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is dark and protruding, but the resolution and lighting do not clearly reveal 'gold-flecked irises'. The iris appears mostly uniform dark/black in this specific crop. While likely present in reality, it is not visually verifiable in this image.
The visible portion of the torso appears thick and robust, consistent with the cylindrical body description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Vivid black and yellow (or orange) warning coloration: glossy black dorsal surface with irregular yellow spots, stripes, or bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is vivid and matches the description perfectly. High contrast between glossy black and bright yellow irregular patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is smooth, moist, and glandular with a glossy, wet-looking appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Specular highlights on the black skin clearly indicate a moist, glossy texture typical of amphibian skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with four digits on forelimbs and five on hindlimbs; digits are blunt and unwebbed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a small portion of a forelimb is visible in the bottom left corner. It is impossible to count the digits or verify if they are unwebbed due to occlusion and framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and shorter than body length, with a rounded tip.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame of this close-up shot.

artifact_observations.location: Yellow patch on top of head/snout
artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow area on the snout has a slightly 'painted' or airbrushed look compared to the more naturalistic gloss of the black skin. The transition between the yellow pigment and the black skin lacks the subtle micro-texture variation seen in high-quality macro photography of amphibians, appearing slightly flat.

Standard depth-of-field blur is present, but the edge of the visible forelimb blends into the background with a slight 'halo' effect, suggesting minor segmentation or generation softness rather than optical bokeh.
